items.action: Rename `buttonRef()` to `controlRef()` on every ds-button template reference, and narrow `.nativeElement` yourself where you read a button-only property off it.
items.appliesWhen: Only code that reads the reference — a template ref used to position or refocus an overlay, or a component that calls it. Nothing changes for a consumer who only uses the element and its inputs, and the property behind the name is the same view child.
items.pitfall: The rename is a compile error and announces itself; the type change may not. `.nativeElement.disabled`, `.form` and `.type` were reachable on `HTMLButtonElement` and are gone from `HTMLElement`, so a read of one fails to compile — but a cast written to silence it then lies at runtime whenever the button carries a destination and really is an anchor.
items.note: The element ds-button renders now follows its destination: an `<a>` when `routerLink` or `href` is set, the `<button>` otherwise. One name and one type had to cover all three, so both were wrong before. Overlay triggers pass `.nativeElement` for positioning and focus, which `HTMLElement` answers.
items.verify: No `buttonRef` remains anywhere in the consumer tree, and every read of `controlRef().nativeElement` either uses only HTMLElement members or narrows with an `instanceof HTMLButtonElement` check.

items.action: Build after upgrading, then rename or mark `override` any member the compiler reports as colliding.
items.appliesWhen: Only a class that extends ButtonComponent, CheckboxComponent, RadioComponent or SwitchComponent. A consumer who uses the elements in a template needs nothing from this item.
items.pitfall: Two of the six new names (`destination`, `resolvedAriaLabel`) are not public API, which is no protection: a redeclared private member fails with TS2415 on the class and TS4114 on the member, and a protected one with TS4114, exactly as a public collision does; a same-named member whose signature differs fails with TS2416 as well, and a method redeclaring a property such as `resolvedAriaLabel` with TS2425 on top.
items.note: ButtonComponent gained `routerLink` and `href`, the two destination inputs; `controlRef`, the view child that replaces `buttonRef`; and `destination`, the computed that decides which of the three elements renders. It also LOST `buttonRef`: a subclass `override buttonRef` now fails with TS4113, and a redeclaration without `override` compiles but is dead. CheckboxComponent, RadioComponent and SwitchComponent each gained `ariaLabel` and `resolvedAriaLabel`.
items.verify: The app builds with no TS2415 or TS2416 naming ButtonComponent, CheckboxComponent, RadioComponent or SwitchComponent, and no member of your subclass is called routerLink, href, controlRef, destination, ariaLabel or resolvedAriaLabel.

informational: `ds-button` takes two new optional inputs, `routerLink` and `href`. Unset, which is the default and what every existing button has, it renders the same `<button type="button">` as before. Set either and it renders an `<a>` instead, with identical styling — the rules are class-based, so nothing keyed to `.button` moves. `type` and `loading` are ignored on a link and say so in dev mode.

A `ds-multi-select` panel filter row now carries `--ds-radius-inner`, so its focus ring is rounded instead of a full-width rectangle. Nothing to change — an `outline` follows the radius of the box it is drawn on, and that row simply had none.

A focus ring is now shaped by its host: the new `--focus-ring-radius` token gives a box that exists only to carry the ring a radius, because an outline follows the `border-radius` of the box it is drawn on and has none of its own. It follows `--ds-radius-inner`, 4px, so a theme that retunes the inner radius moves these rings with it. `ds-checkbox`, `ds-radio` and `ds-switch` pick it up, so their keyboard focus ring is rounded instead of square. Nothing to change — the resting state of all three is untouched, and a host with its own radius keeps it.

A clickable `ds-table` row, a `ds-tree` row and a `ds-list` activator now carry `--focus-ring-radius`, so their keyboard focus ring is rounded instead of square. Nothing to change: the table row and the list activator paint no background of their own, so there the radius shapes only the ring; a `ds-tree` row paints its own hover, pressed and selected fill, and that fill now takes the same rounded corners.

A field marked `disabled` no longer paints its `data-field-state`. An `error`, `warning` or `success` state used to out-rank the disabled look in `ds-input`, `ds-textarea`, `ds-select`, `ds-multi-select`, `ds-autocomplete`, `ds-date-picker`, `ds-time-picker`, `ds-color-picker` and `ds-otp-input`, on specificity alone, so a field left invalid and then disabled kept a red border and fill it could not act on. Nothing to change — `data-field-state` is set the same way and means the same thing, and a read-only field still paints it, because `readonly` is submitted where `disabled` is not.

`ds-field-group[invalid]` keeps its error border while hovered and while holding focus. Both `:hover` and `:focus-within` used to out-rank `.invalid` on specificity and repaint the border, which is the group's only error affordance because a segment's own label and message are hidden. Its focus halo now takes the error tint, through the new `--ds-field-group-focus-shadow-error` (default `--ds-field-focus-shadow-error`). Nothing to change — a valid group hovers and focuses as before, and a stylesheet that set `--ds-field-group-focus-shadow` still gets it on the valid state.

`ds-stat variant="error"` now actually recolours the value. `:host(.error) .value` tied `.stat .value` on specificity and lost on source order, so the variant painted nothing; error now moves the `--_stat-value-color` resolver. Nothing to change, and a stylesheet setting `--ds-stat-value-color` still wins over it, exactly as before.

`ds-breadcrumbs`: `BreadcrumbItem` takes an optional `ariaLabel`, and a crumb with an `icon` and no `label` needs it: that shape rendered a link with no accessible name. Add `ariaLabel` to any icon-only crumb — the usual home crumb — and the component dev-warns while one is missing. Nothing derives from `icon`, because a glyph id is not a word for the user.

`ds-sidenav-footer`'s collapse button carries an `aria-label`, and its label reads `Expand` while the rail is collapsed rather than always `Collapse`. Nothing to change; a stylesheet that keyed off the text content of `.row .label` is the one exception, and none is expected.

`--focus-ring` is a two-shadow LIST for `box-shadow`, not a value for `outline` — worth knowing because putting it in an `outline` fails silently and takes the ring with it. A `var()` that cannot substitute is invalid at computed-value time, so the property computes back to its initial value instead of being dropped, and it still out-ranks the library's own `:where(:focus-visible)` ring by specificity: the element ends up with no indicator at all. For an outline use `--focus-ring-width`, `--focus-ring-color` and `--focus-ring-offset`, or just let the global ring do it. Nothing in the package was affected; this is the shape to avoid in consumer stylesheets.

`ds-checkbox`, `ds-radio` and `ds-switch` take an optional `ariaLabel`, for the case where the control renders no visible label — no `label` and nothing projected. Until now such a control had no accessible name and no way to be given one; `ds-select` and `ds-number-stepper` already took the same input. Nothing to change unless you have a label-less one, and setting it ALONGSIDE a label overrides what the label says, which is the ARIA rule and rarely what you want.
